submission.natural_language_explanation: openai-community/gpt2 L1/H2 is a sequence-start readout, not a content detector: from the second token on it attends back to the text's first token (0.99, 0.87 and 0.65-0.73 of its attention at tokens 1, 2 and 3 of ordinary prose; 0.83-0.997 over 3,000 random token pairs) and its write there is far from its mean for every one of the 50,257 vocabulary tokens (11.6-13.7 above its 3.2 floor at position 0), so its strength is a function of position alone. Every text of two or more tokens therefore peaks at tokens 1-7 (296 of 300 prompts at token 4) between 11.5 and 13.74 above the floor, against an active line of 3.435, so no text of two or more tokens is predicted inactive (a one-token text is unmeasured) - min 12.00 over 7,500 varied prompts (prose, code, CJK, random token sequences) and 11.54 for the quietest opening token - and only the height depends on the opening: a run of space tokens at the start gives the scan maximum 13.741 at token 4, an ordinary opening 12.0-13.3, changing every word after the opening changes nothing, mid-text indentation, newlines and whitespace runs add nothing, and after the opening the write decays with distance from the start to zero at tokens 76-110 and rises to a second, ~6 band at tokens 150-250.

rival_explanations: Whitespace-run detector: every top example peaks on a run of space tokens, so the unit fires on space runs wherever they sit - a deeply indented code line in mid-document should fire as strongly as a text's opening, and single-spaced prose should not fire at all.

Line-start detector: the peak in every top example sits on the leading whitespace of a source line, so the unit fires at the start of each line after a newline, and a multi-line text should fire once per line at a similar height.
